The original always listens on port 3000 and always calls OpenRouter's address, so the copy that produced these cases listens on PORT and prints it, falling back to 3000, a two-line change in src/index.ts, and passes OPENAI_BASE_URL to ChatOpenAI as its base URL, falling back to OpenRouter's, a one-line change in src/services/openRouterService.ts. No OpenRouter key was available, so the answers were recorded from Ollama 0.40.11 through its OpenAI-compatible API, with gpt-oss:20b standing in for arcee-ai/trinity-large-preview:free, the only model the configuration offers, and wrapped in OpenRouter's documented response format without the stand-in's reasoning, while the requests keep the model and the routing the program sends. Each turn calls the model twice, once to extract the intent and once to write the message, and both ask for a json_schema response format, which the cases check by its type and its schema's properties and required fields, as the multiple MCP tools lesson's do. The intent prompt carries the current date, which the cases check by its ISO shape, so the replayed dates stay those of the day of the recording, 2026-10-27, and no case relies on the two appointments the service starts with, which fall on the day the server starts. The route answers the graph's final state, which the cases check field by field: the messages in LangChain's serialized form, their ids by the UUID version 4 shape, and the fields no node set by their absence. The rejected key is synthesized from OpenRouter's documented error format, and the error it leaves in the state, which is the runtime's own message, is checked as any non-empty text, in the answer and in the message prompt. The message shorter than the schema allows is synthesized from a recorded one, and so is the cancellation at another time that makes the tests fail. Fastify's error bodies are checked by status code, statusCode, and error, with any non-empty message, because the validation messages come from Ajv, except the unknown routes, whose messages are short and checked exactly. The handler's 500 answer is never checked, because every node catches its own failures. The tests program is checked by its requests and by whether it succeeds or fails, never by its report.
